name: Tring
tagline: Write a voice agent once in YAML and run it on any speech architecture
summary: Tring is an open-source voice agent stack built from lessons learned across more than a million production telephony calls. One YAML agent contract runs on cascade, speech-to-speech or hybrid runtimes with the same tools, analytics and cost attribution, so changing architecture is a config change. The default pipeline runs entirely on local open models, and four latency primitives make dead air during tool calls structurally impossible.

metrics.source: README.md: Define a voice agent once, in plain YAML, and run it on any of three architectures without rewriting anything

features: One agent contract runs on cascade (STT, LLM, TTS), speech-to-speech or hybrid runtimes
Tool calls must declare what the caller hears while they run, so there is no dead air
Playback ledger tracks heard versus unheard text, so the model never cites words a caller interrupted
Per-language routing of STT, TTS and LLM for callers who code-switch
Cost meter with exact versus estimated flags and a cost-per-outcome report; Studio for building, testing and replaying calls in the browser
how_it_works: An AgentSpec in YAML declares the persona, tools, language policy and runtime routing, and a RuntimeAdapter runs it on the chosen architecture.
The model answers in a speak-then-tool-call envelope, and a character-level parser streams the speech to TTS while the tool call is still being generated.
Every runtime emits the same SessionEvent stream, so cost metering, analytics and transports subscribe to it without knowing which runtime is underneath.
quickstart:
pip install "tring[transports]"
tring studio
# opens at http://localhost:8900

PyPI version 0.4.1 confirmed via pypi.org JSON; GitHub latest release v0.4.1 (the demo mp4 is attached to v0.4.0 only). The README contains no benchmark latency or cost-saving numbers, so metrics are track record and zero-cost facts; no latency figure was invented. docs/launch-posts.md says 'hundreds of thousands' of calls while the README says 'more than a million'; I used the README figure, owner should confirm. Install command in the README is pip install tring; tring studio needs the transports extra. Not verified: the README diagram annotation '~0ms to first audio' is a diagram label, not a measurement, so it is not used.
